theme: Endothelial nitric oxide-cGMP control of vascular tone
story: The centre is endothelial NO production: eNOS activation and its trafficking (NOSTRIN, NOSIP), the BH4 cofactor and L-arginine substrate supply, and positive/negative regulation of NO synthesis, feeding NO-cGMP signalling and cGMP effects that relax vascular smooth muscle. Opposing vasoconstrictor inputs (endothelin, catecholamines, arterial smooth muscle contraction) and counter-regulation of guanylyl cyclase signalling set the balance. The downstream readouts are systemic and pulmonary blood pressure, vascular permeability and renal sodium and water excretion, so the cluster as a whole describes how NO tunes vessel tone and blood pressure.

theme: Notch receptor intracellular domain transcriptional signalling
story: The core is the canonical Notch output: the intracellular domains of NOTCH1-4 enter the nucleus and drive HLH target genes (Notch-HLH pathway, hallmark Notch signalling, positive regulation of target transcription). Oncogenic NOTCH1 PEST and HD+PEST mutants and FBXW7 loss represent the same pathway made constitutive by stabilising the intracellular domain, while negative regulation of Notch signalling supplies the brakes. Together it is the Notch signalling axis from receptor cleavage product to transcription, in normal and cancer-driven form.

theme: Glutamate and GABA reuptake and recycling at synapses
story: The centre is clearance of the main excitatory and inhibitory transmitters: glutamate reuptake by EAAT transporters (with D-aspartate as a substrate), GABA reuptake and import, and SLC-mediated neurotransmitter transport. Astrocytic glutamate-glutamine uptake and intracellular glutamate homeostasis recycle transmitter back to neurons, and vesicular loading (VGLUT3/SLC17A8) refills synaptic vesicles. Disease entries (SLC1A3 episodic ataxia, SLC17A8 deafness) show the consequences of failure; the cluster as a whole is the transporter system that terminates and recycles amino acid neurotransmission.

theme: Axon guidance of peripheral and monoaminergic neurons
story: The centre is axon guidance proper: anterior/posterior guidance, chemorepulsion, and positive and negative regulation of axon extension during guidance. Specific neuron classes (serotonergic, dopaminergic, sympathetic) and innervation-directed axonogenesis show where these cues are applied, while dorsal root ganglion development and peripheral neuron differentiation provide the developmental context. Together it describes how developing neurons, especially peripheral ones, extend and steer axons to their targets.

theme: Ionotropic glutamate receptor excitatory transmission and its presynaptic tuning
story: The centre is fast excitatory transmission through AMPA and kainate receptors (Ca- and Na-permeable kainate receptor activation, AMPA receptor activity), with receptor clustering and diffusion trapping positioning receptors at synapses and shaping short-term plasticity. Presynaptic kainate receptor function, presynaptic depolarisation and Ca channel opening, and G-protein brakes (Gbeta/gamma inhibition of Ca channels, GIRK activation, extrasynaptic GABA) tune release. Kainic acid response and hippocampal neuron apoptosis capture the excitotoxic downside of over-activating this system.

theme: LXR-ABCA1 cholesterol efflux, HDL biogenesis and foam cells
story: The centre is reverse cholesterol transport from cells: LXR (NR1H3/NR1H2) induces ABC transporters that efflux cholesterol and phospholipid onto apolipoprotein A-I to assemble HDL, with Tangier disease (defective ABCA1) as its failure. The opposing side is cholesterol loading - oxidised LDL responses, cholesterol import and storage, pinocytosis - which drives macrophage foam cell formation, with positive and negative regulators on both sides. The cluster as a whole describes the cellular balance of cholesterol uptake versus efflux that decides whether macrophages become atherogenic foam cells.

theme: Actin filament turnover powering lamellipodial cell migration
story: The centre is dynamic actin remodelling: filament severing, depolymerisation, barbed-end capping, restraint of Arp2/3 nucleation, and crosslinking into networks (the cofilin/gelsolin machinery). These drive lamellipodium morphogenesis, cell extension and actin-based contraction for substrate-dependent migration. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins is the apoptotic dismantling of the same filament system; overall the cluster is the actin turnover cycle that moves a cell's leading edge.

theme: Rho GTPase-guided actin remodelling shaping cell protrusions
story: The core is actin filament dynamics - severing, capping, depolymerisation, crosslinking, Arp2/3 restraint, parallel bundle and network formation - which builds and dismantles filopodia (positive and negative regulation). Upstream signals (RHOF cycle, Rho activation of citron kinase, EPHB forward signalling) direct this machinery, and its outputs include cell polarity and shape, postsynaptic actin organisation in spines, and coupling to microtubule stability. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins is the apoptotic teardown of the same structures; the cluster as a whole is about how signalling sculpts the actin cytoskeleton into protrusions and cell shape.

theme: Stress-induced cellular senescence and its secretory phenotype
story: The centre is entry into senescence: oncogene-induced, oxidative-stress-induced and stress-induced premature senescence and positive regulation of senescence, with BMI1/USP16 control of the CDKN2A locus setting how readily cells exit the cycle. Blocking re-entry (negative regulation of G0-to-G1 transition and of fibroblast proliferation) locks in the arrest, while dampened p53-driven apoptosis, DNA damage signalling and stress kinase cascades explain why senescent cells survive rather than die. The SASP is the inflammatory output, so the cluster covers senescence from trigger to stable arrest to secretory consequence.

theme: Immediate-early transcriptional response to stress and mitogens
story: The centre is the rapid inducible gene programme triggered by external stimuli: TNF-alpha/NF-kB targets, UV response genes (up and down), phorbol ester (PMA) response and NR4A-enriched growth-factor immediate-early genes. Kinase signals (p38 MAPK, PI3K-AKT-mTOR) and nitric oxide relay the stimuli, and cell cycle/growth arrest is one of the main outcomes. Together it describes a generic cellular alarm response that converts diverse insults and mitogens into a shared early transcriptional burst.

theme: DNA glycosylase-initiated base excision repair and its defects
story: The centre is the first steps of base excision repair: DNA glycosylases recognise and excise damaged purines and pyrimidines, APEX1 displaces them to process the abasic site, and AP sites are resolved by single-nucleotide replacement and single-strand break repair. Most other members are disease variants of the glycosylases themselves (OGG1, NTHL1, MUTYH, NEIL1, NEIL3) defective in localisation, binding or processing, plus NEIL3's role in unhooking interstrand crosslinks. The cluster as a whole is the glycosylase-driven BER pathway and what goes wrong when it is broken.

theme: E2F-driven G1/S cell-cycle transcription
story: The centre is the E2F transcriptional programme: E2F targets, G1/S-specific transcription and the E2F transcription factor network that licenses DNA replication. Its repressors (DREAM complex, p107/p130-HDAC1, E2F6) hold these genes off in quiescence, and positive regulation of G1/S and G2/M transitions plus the generic cell cycle and replication modules capture the proliferative output. The cluster as a whole is the transcriptional switch that commits cells to divide.

theme: EGFR/ERBB2 adaptor signalling to PLC-gamma and PI3K
story: The centre is signalling from activated EGFR and ERBB2 receptors through their docking adaptors: SHC1, GRB2, GRB7 and the GAB1 signalosome, which connect to PLC-gamma1 and PI3K and thus to phosphoinositide signalling. ERBB2 additional outputs (PTK6, cell motility) and the analogous PLC-gamma cascade from FGFR4 extend the picture, while inhibition of overexpressed EGFR reflects its regulation. Together it describes how ErbB-family receptor tyrosine kinases translate phosphotyrosines into lipid second messengers and growth/motility signals.

theme: Telomere capping, protection and recombination-based maintenance
story: The centre is protecting chromosome ends: telomere capping, packaging of telomere ends, protection from NHEJ and suppression of DSB repair there, and subtelomeric heterochromatin. Telomere length is maintained by telomerase (negatively regulated), semi-conservative replication, and the recombination-based ALT route (D-loop disassembly, t-circle formation), which ATRX/DAXX normally inhibit and whose loss enables ALT in cancer. Linked DNA processing (strand elongation, mitotic recombination, cohesion) and negative regulation of senescence show what the system ultimately prevents - end fusions and replicative senescence.

theme: Transporter-mediated drug disposition (ADME)
story: The centre is membrane transport of xenobiotics: OATP/SLCO sodium-independent organic anion uptake, xenobiotic export and transmembrane transport, including across the blood-brain barrier. Drug ADME pathways (atorvastatin, prednisone, aspirin, ciprofloxacin) are concrete cases in which these transporters set absorption and clearance, and flavone and glycoside handling extends the same transporters to dietary compounds. The cluster is about how carrier proteins move drugs and foreign organic anions into and out of cells and tissues.

theme: Cardiac action potential and conduction system
story: The centre is the cardiomyocyte action potential: phase 0 rapid sodium-driven depolarisation and the phase 2 calcium plateau, with regulation of ventricular and atrial membrane depolarisation. Conduction through the His-Purkinje system and cell-cell signalling in cardiac conduction propagate this excitation, and regulation of heart rate and of contraction are its outputs. Together the cluster describes the electrical excitation and propagation that time each heartbeat.

theme: RIG-I/MDA5 sensing and type I interferon antiviral induction
story: The centre is cytosolic viral RNA sensing by RIG-I-like receptors (DDX58/IFIH1) responding to dsRNA, signalling via TRAF3/TRAF6 to TBK1/IKK-epsilon, which activate IRF3/IRF7 and NF-kB to induce type I interferon (TLR3 and FADD/RIP1 routes converge on the same outputs). Negative regulators and OTU deubiquitinases restrain the pathway, while ISG15 conjugation and IFN-stimulated genes form the effector arm. Viral evasion and modulation (RSV, SARS-CoV-1/2) show the pathway as a battleground; the whole cluster is the innate antiviral interferon circuit.

theme: Netrin signalling in axon guidance and collateral sprouting
story: The centre is netrin-1 signalling: the netrin-activated pathway, its repulsive signals via UNC5 receptors and second messengers (Ca, cAMP) that set attraction versus repulsion. These control positive and negative regulation of axon extension, chemorepulsion and anterior/posterior guidance, and also collateral branch sprouting. Dorsal root ganglion development places it in sensory neuron wiring; the cluster describes how a single guidance cue steers and branches axons.

theme: Metal ion and redox stress response via metallothioneins
story: The centre is MTF1-driven induction of metallothioneins, which bind and detoxify metals, alongside copper detoxification. Responses to many metal ions (zinc, copper, iron, manganese, cobalt, lead, mercury, selenium) are the triggers, and redox handling (HMOX1 regulation, redox state, hydrogen peroxide and oxidoreductase restraint) deals with the oxidative stress metals provoke. Chaperone-mediated autophagy regulation is a peripheral protective layer; overall the cluster is the cell's defence against metal overload and the oxidative damage it causes.

theme: FGF receptor activation and downstream adaptor signalling
story: The centre is FGFR1-4 activation: ligand binding by the IIIb/IIIc splice isoforms and betaKlotho-dependent endocrine FGF binding. Activated receptors signal through FRS2 and SHC adaptors to the MAPK cascade and through PLC-gamma, with each receptor represented. Oncogenic activating point mutants of FGFR1-4 show the same pathway made constitutive in disease; the cluster is FGF signalling from receptor to effector.

theme: Glycolytic flux control and cellular energy buffering
story: The centre is glucose catabolism through glycolysis: hexokinase entry (HK1 deficiency), fructose 1,6- and 2,6-bisphosphate metabolism as the main PFK regulatory node, and fermentation to lactate. Mitochondrial ADP/ATP exchange and the creatine/phosphocreatine system distribute and buffer the ATP produced, and resveratrol response sits at the metabolic-regulation margin. Together the cluster is about how cells generate ATP from glucose and shuttle and buffer that energy.

theme: Urea cycle and ornithine-citrulline-arginine metabolism
story: The centre is the hepatic urea cycle: NAGS-activated carbamoyl phosphate synthesis, OTC forming citrulline, aspartate incorporation and arginine synthesis and cleavage back to ornithine. Mitochondrial ornithine transport (SLC25A15, HHH syndrome) and cationic amino acid transport move intermediates, transcriptional repression of urea cycle enzymes controls flux, and NAGS and OTC variants are the inborn errors. The cluster is the nitrogen-disposal cycle and its disorders of hyperammonaemia.

theme: Semaphorin and netrin repulsive axon guidance
story: The centre is repulsive guidance cues: Sema3A-plexin signalling through CRMPs, PAK and inhibition of integrin adhesion, plus netrin repulsion, all collapsing or turning growth cones (chemorepulsion). These cues regulate axon extension, collateral sprouting (positive and negative) and inhibit neuron projection regeneration, applied to serotonergic and sympathetic axons and innervation. The cluster describes how semaphorin and netrin signals shape axon paths and branching during development and limit regrowth after injury.

theme: Renal epithelial salt, potassium and magnesium transport
story: The centre is cation-chloride cotransport in the kidney: NKCC2 (Bartter syndrome), NCC (Gitelman syndrome) and KCC3 (ACCPN), driving transepithelial chloride and renal sodium transport, with regulation of sodium transporter activity and potassium channels and import. Paracellular transport through tight junctions (claudin-based, calcium-independent adhesion) and magnesium transport and homeostasis complete the tubular handling of divalent cations. Hypotonic response, anion homeostasis and inositol transporters reflect the cell-volume side of the same transporters; overall it is electrolyte reabsorption and cell volume control.

theme: Semaphorin-3A and netrin guidance of axon extension
story: The centre is Sema3A-plexin signalling (CRMPs, PAK-dependent repulsion, inhibition of integrin adhesion) together with netrin signalling, especially its repulsive arm. These cues act on axon guidance, axonogenesis toward innervation targets and positive regulation of axon extension, including sympathetic neuron projections. The cluster as a whole describes how secreted guidance cues steer growing axons.

theme: B cell identity and B cell receptor activation
story: The centre is the mature B cell programme captured by expression modules: B cell surface signatures, naive and memory B cell sets and the BCR signalling module (CD79A, STAP1, BTLA restraint), with positive regulation of BCR signalling. Plasma cell and immunoglobulin modules and lymphocyte activation in organised lymphoid tissue describe the progression to antibody secretion, while generic T and B lymphocyte modules provide context. The cluster as a whole marks B lymphocyte identity and its antigen-driven activation.

theme: Amino acid catabolism and glycine conjugation of organic acids
story: The centre is degradation of amino acids: phenylalanine/tyrosine catabolism (phenylketonuria), histidine, threonine, glycine, proline and glutamine-family metabolism, much of it mitochondrial and peroxisomal, plus glyoxylate and glycine/proline synthesis. Glycine and glutamine conjugation of benzoate, salicylate and phenylacetate uses the same amino acid pool to detoxify aromatic acids, and aldehyde, dicarboxylic acid and pyrimidine catabolism extend the organic acid theme. Many broad (often obsolete) GO terms simply enclose this; the cluster is the liver's organic and amino acid breakdown network.

theme: Eye development: retina, lens and ocular vasculature
story: The centre is retinal development: optic cup and retina morphogenesis, layer formation, and specification and maintenance of photoreceptors (rods, cones, outer segments, cilia), amacrine and bipolar cells and the pigment epithelium. Anterior eye structures (lens fibre differentiation and transparency, cornea, iris, eyelid, pigmentation) and the ocular vasculature (retinal vessel formation, hyaloid regression, blood-retinal/blood-brain barrier via Norrin/WNT-FZD4) complete the organ. A few members (vagina development, a neurotrophic BTM module, gap junction transport) are peripheral; overall the cluster builds the camera-type eye.

theme: Visual retinoid cycle and its inherited defects
story: The centre is the retinoid (visual) cycle that regenerates 11-cis-retinal for rods and cones, built on vitamin A metabolism. Loss-of-function defects of its enzymes and transporters (LRAT, RDH5, RDH12, ABCA4, STRA6) and retinoid disease events are the main disorder branch, while A2E formation and high-light responses represent toxic by-products that degrade the retina. The cluster is the chromophore recycling system of vision and how its failure causes retinal dystrophy.

theme: Presynaptic G-protein modulation of neurotransmitter release
story: The centre is presynaptic control of release: Gi-coupled metabotropic glutamate and GABA-B receptors act via Gbeta/gamma to inhibit voltage-gated Ca channels and open GIRK channels, lowering presynaptic Ca and membrane potential. Presynaptic kainate receptors and depolarisation-driven Ca entry act in the opposite direction, and the outputs are positive and negative regulation of synaptic vesicle exocytosis and of glutamate and GABA secretion. The cluster as a whole describes how presynaptic receptors tune how much transmitter terminals release.

theme: mRNA 3'-end processing, deadenylation and decay
story: The centre is the poly(A) tail's life cycle: co-transcriptional cleavage and polyadenylation (including intronless pre-mRNAs) builds the tail, and deadenylation and poly(A) shortening start its removal. Decapping, 5'-to-3' exonucleolytic decay, deadenylation-independent decay and P-body assembly complete degradation, while 3'-UTR-mediated stabilisation counteracts it and maternal mRNA clearance is a developmental instance. The cluster describes how mRNA ends are made and then used to control mRNA lifespan.

theme: Excitatory amino acid and GABA transport and recycling
story: The centre is uptake of acidic amino acid transmitters: EAAT-mediated glutamate reuptake and L- and D-aspartate import (SLC1A1, SLC1A3), regulation of glutamate import and GABA reuptake and import. Astrocytic glutamate-glutamine cycling, intracellular glutamate homeostasis and GABA synthesis and metabolism close the loop by regenerating transmitter, and vesicular loading by VGLUT3 sits at the release end. Disease variants (SLC1A1 in schizophrenia and dicarboxylic aminoaciduria, SLC1A3 episodic ataxia, SLC17A8 deafness) show the cost of failure; the cluster is the transporter-based clearance and recycling of glutamate, aspartate and GABA.

theme: Mitotic spindle assembly, centrosome maturation and spindle checkpoint
story: The centre is building the mitotic spindle: Aurora A activation by TPX2 and its regulation (FBXL7, PHLDA1), PLK1 activity at G2/M, recruitment of centrosome proteins and NuMA with loss of Nlp during centrosome maturation, and EML4/NUDC spindle formation. The spindle assembly checkpoint (MAD2 amplification from unattached kinetochores, positive and negative regulation) and chromosome localisation ensure attachment before anaphase. The hallmark mitotic spindle and mitotic cell division terms summarise a cluster about assembling a bipolar spindle and policing chromosome segregation.

theme: Renal and hormonal regulation of systemic blood pressure
story: The centre is endocrine blood pressure control: renin-angiotensin regulation of blood volume and angiotensin signalling, vasopressin, and renal control of peripheral resistance, raising pressure. Counter-regulation lowers it through sodium excretion, urine volume and reduced vasoconstriction, with natriuretic peptide (receptor guanylyl cyclase) signalling regulated, and lung pressure as a related bed. Together it is the kidney-hormone axis that sets blood volume and arterial pressure.

theme: Myoblast and satellite cell control of muscle regeneration
story: The centre is the decision of myogenic precursors between proliferating and differentiating: positive and negative regulation of myoblast proliferation and negative regulation of myoblast, myotube and satellite-cell differentiation. Satellite cell maintenance and somatic stem cell division sustain the reservoir, while myoblast migration and fusion rebuild fibres during regeneration. Broader negative regulation of muscle tissue and organ development frames the cluster as the control of skeletal muscle growth and repair from its stem cells.

theme: tRNA maturation, modification and aminoacylation
story: The centre is charging tRNAs: cytosolic and mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase activity and the aminoacyl-tRNA metabolism that ensures translational fidelity. tRNA maturation (3'-end processing, intron splicing) and anticodon-loop modifications (wybutosine at G37 of tRNA-Phe, wobble uridine thiolation and guanine modification) make tRNAs functional and accurate decoders. Translation termination sits at the other end of decoding; overall the cluster is the preparation of tRNAs for accurate protein synthesis.

theme: Retroviral replication and host restriction of retroelements
story: The centre is the HIV/retroviral life cycle: binding and entry, uncoating, minus- and plus-strand reverse transcription, Vpr-assisted nuclear import of the pre-integration complex, integration, and dead-end 2-LTR and autointegration circles. Host defences oppose it - APOBEC3G cytidine deamination (countered by Vif), suppression of viral transcription and replication, nucleic-acid clearance, LRRFIP1-driven interferon, siRNA processing - and HUSH, KRAB-ZFP and ChAHP silencing of endogenous retroelements extend restriction to the genome's own retrotransposons. Viral latency, frameshifting, HCMV events and RNA editing round out a cluster about viral genome replication versus host genome defence.

theme: Integrated stress response and ER unfolded protein response
story: The centre is translational control under stress: eIF2-alpha kinases (PERK, GCN2 for amino acid deficiency, HRI for heme deficiency) repress translation initiation, with selective translation of stress genes. The ER unfolded protein response branches (PERK, IRE1, positively and negatively regulated) and UFMylation manage ER load, and when stress persists the outputs shift to ER-stress-induced apoptosis, including pancreatic beta cell death. The cluster is the cell's stress-to-translation-to-fate decision system.

theme: Hexosamine and sialic acid supply for N-glycosylation
story: The centre is amino sugar metabolism feeding glycosylation: the hexosamine pathway (GFPT1) making UDP-GlcNAc from fructose 6-phosphate, sialic acid synthesis (GNE) to CMP-Neu5Ac, and mannose and UDP-glucose/dolichyl-glucose donors. These supply N-linked glycosylation and N-glycan processing (ALG14, MOGS, MAN1B1), whose defects cause congenital myasthenic syndromes and CDGs, while lysosomal oligosaccharide and sialic acid catabolism recycle the products. The cluster is the sugar supply and turnover chain behind protein N-glycosylation.

theme: Erythroid heme-iron metabolism and blood gas transport
story: The centre is the red cell's oxygen machinery: heme biosynthesis (porphyrin steps, mitochondrial ABC transporters, ABCB6), iron supply via transferrin cycling, ferroportin, DMT1 and ceruloplasmin (with their hemochromatosis/anaemia defects), and heme scavenging and transport. Erythrocyte differentiation and haemoglobin synthesis use these, and the functional output is oxygen, CO2 and NO transport and gas exchange. Rh glycoproteins (ammonium transport, Rh-null anaemia) and Fe-S cluster assembly are adjacent red-cell membrane and iron-use processes; overall it is iron-to-heme-to-haemoglobin-to-gas exchange.

theme: Oxidative metabolism of ethanol and dietary toxins
story: The centre is ethanol oxidation by alcohol and aldehyde dehydrogenases and CYP enzymes, together with primary alcohol catabolism. The same cytochrome P450 system bioactivates and detoxifies mycotoxins such as aflatoxin (a polyketide) and catabolises other toxins, and steroid metabolism represents its endogenous substrates. The cluster as a whole is phase I oxidative handling of alcohol and ingested toxins.

theme: Cell-cycle progression and DNA damage checkpoints
story: The centre is the cell-cycle engine: RB-E2F control of G1/S transcription (DREAM, p107/p130, E2F6, RB mutants), cyclin D/E-CDK activity and its inhibition (CDK4/6 drugs, p27/p21 degradation), then G2/M cyclin A/B-CDK1, PLK1, MASTL, NEK kinases and mitotic progression. Checkpoints overlay this - Chk1/Chk2 inactivation of cyclin B-CDK1, Cdc25A degradation, p53-driven G2 arrest, replication and G1/S checkpoints. Many proliferation modules (E2F targets, G2M hallmark, cell cycle BTMs) summarise the same programme; the cluster is the whole proliferative cycle and its brakes.

theme: Cohesin-mediated sister chromatid cohesion
story: The centre is the cohesin cycle: loading onto chromatin, establishment of cohesion during replication, maintenance especially at centromeres in mitosis and meiosis. Resolution of cohesion and separation of sister chromatids end the cycle at anaphase, and chromatin looping reflects cohesin's interphase role in genome folding. The cluster is how cohesin holds sister chromatids together and releases them.

theme: Phase I/II detoxification of ethanol, aldehydes and xenobiotics
story: The centre is xenobiotic metabolism: cytochrome P450 oxidation of ethanol, aflatoxin and other mycotoxins/polyketides and toxins, with aldehyde detoxification clearing the reactive aldehydes these reactions produce. Cytosolic sulfonation provides a phase II conjugation step, and steroid metabolism shows the endogenous substrates of the same enzymes. Together the cluster is the liver's oxidative and conjugative detoxification chain.

theme: Insulin signalling to glycogen and glucose handling
story: The centre is insulin receptor signalling: IRS activation and AKT2, with signal attenuation and negative regulation of insulin response (insulin resistance) as the brakes. The metabolic outputs are glycogen synthesis versus glycogenolysis and glucose uptake, while glucokinase and its regulatory protein (with MODY2 when defective) control glucose sensing and phosphorylation in liver and beta cells. The cluster as a whole is hormonal control of glucose storage as glycogen.

theme: RNA polymerase I transcription of ribosomal RNA
story: The centre is the Pol I transcription cycle on rDNA: preinitiation complex assembly, promoter opening and escape, elongation and termination. Chromatin regulators set rDNA activity - B-WICH and CSB/G9a positively, NoRC negatively - while Pol III 5S rRNA transcription and ITS2 cleavage of the precursor connect to the rest of ribosome RNA production; Pol II elongation is a peripheral member. The cluster is the production of ribosomal RNA for ribosome biogenesis.

theme: Phase I and phase II drug and xenobiotic biotransformation
story: The centre is xenobiotic metabolism by oxidation - CYP2E1, CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation/dealkylation, FMO oxidation of nucleophiles, oxidative demethylation - and by conjugation through methylation (TPMT), acetylation and sulfonation. Substrates include drugs (paracetamol), aflatoxin, alkaloids, phenylpropanoids, monoterpenoids and benzene compounds, and TPMT and FMO3 deficiencies show the pharmacogenetic consequences. The cluster is the enzymatic toolkit that chemically modifies foreign compounds for elimination.

theme: Nucleotide sugar synthesis and Golgi transport for glycosylation
story: The centre is production of activated sugar donors - UDP-GlcNAc via the hexosamine pathway (GFPT1), GDP-fucose, UDP-glucuronate, CMP-sialic acid (GNE), mannose and UDP-glucose. SLC35 transporters (A1, A2, A3, C1) and SLC33A1 move these donors and acetyl-CoA into the ER/Golgi lumen, and their defects cause congenital disorders of glycosylation and related syndromes. The cluster is the supply line that feeds glycosyltransferases in the secretory pathway.

theme: Actin polymerization dynamics driving leading-edge motility
story: The centre is the actin treadmill at the leading edge: polymerisation versus depolymerisation, severing, barbed-end capping, Arp2/3 restraint and crosslinking into networks. These build lamellipodia, ruffles and pseudopodia and localise proteins to the leading edge, producing actin polymerisation-driven motility and substrate-dependent extension with actomyosin contraction. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins dismantles the same system in apoptosis; the cluster is the force-generating actin machinery of cell crawling.

theme: Antigen presentation and cytotoxic T and NK cell recognition
story: The centre is MHC antigen processing and presentation: class I loading via proteasome and ER/phagosome cross-presentation, class II endosomal processing and peptide assembly, and lipid/MHC Ib presentation. Recognition of these complexes by CD8 T cells and NK cells (KIR and activating receptors, cytotoxicity, granzyme killing) is the effector side, balanced by costimulation, anergy, tolerance and protection from NK killing, with dendritic cells as presenters. HIV Nef and Vpu downregulation of MHC I, CD4, CD8 and CD28 shows viral escape; the cluster as a whole is immune surveillance of infected or abnormal cells through antigen display.
